items.title: Andrew Morgan Interview, 1961-07-04
items.q: So then I played with Young Morgan around here for a few years.

ctx.x: with Sam. So, my brother was playing up here on Liberty Street. I just forget the name of the place. But anyway, well, Jim Robison was in the band. In your little band? Yeah. And that's Young Morgan. Yeah, the young one. Sidney Brown, that was the bass player. And Johnny Deve was playing banjo. No, I think we had at that time on the drum, Rudolph. I just can't think of Rudolph's last name.

Is that Bollier? Bollier? Bollier, that's, yeah. Big Rudolph. Yeah. So, um... He'd been sick, had a stroke some time ago. Well, that's what I heard. But we interviewed him about a month ago, and he looks in pretty good health. So, he'd like to play again now. That's good. And they'd be able to start in again.

So, uh, he and this Young Morgan band, well, Jim Robison had a brother they called Sam. I've heard of him, but never got to know him. Well, that's the fellow that I take in his place, you see. Uh, seems like, uh, that they had heard me play, and they're, uh, they're like my style of playing. And then I joined the band. So then I played with Young Morgan around here for a few years. And after my brother Sam, he was sick, and, uh, he was not able to keep up a band by himself. So then he came over to my brother…
